Students continuing to PHYS 1B/1BL will also need MATH 10B or 20B.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or 20A. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1A and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Second quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course geared toward life-science majors. Electric fields, magnetic fields, DC and AC circuitry. PHYS 1B and 1BL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1A or 2A, and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1B. Experiments in electricity and magnetism. Program or materials fee may apply. PHYS 1B and 1BL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1A or 2A, 1AL or 2BL, and MATH 10B or 20B. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Waves, Optics, and Modern Physics
courses.description: Third quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course geared toward life-science majors. The physics of oscillations and waves, vibrating strings and sound, and the interaction of light with matter as illustrated through optics and quantum mechanics. Examples from biology, sports, medicine, and current events. PHYS 1C and 1CL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1B or 2B, and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Waves, Optics, and Modern Physics Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1C. Experiments in waves, optics, and modern physics. Program or materials fee may apply. PHYS 1C and 1CL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1B or 2B, 1BL or 2CL, and MATH 10B or 20B. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1C.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Mechanics
courses.description: A calculus-based science-engineering general physics course covering vectors, motion in one and two dimensions, Newton’s first and second laws, work and energy, conservation of energy, linear momentum, collisions, rotational kinematics, rotational dynamics, equilibrium of rigid bodies, oscillations, gravitation. Students continuing to PHYS 2B/4B will also need MATH 20B. Students will not receive credit for both PHYS 2A and PHYS 2AR.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A-B or 20A or 20B or 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 2A covering charge and matter, the electric field, Gauss’s law, electric potential, capacitors and dielectrics, current and resistance, electromotive force and circuits, the magnetic field, Ampere’s law, Faraday’s law, inductance, electromagnetic oscillations, alternating currents and Maxwell’s equations. Students continuing to PHYS 2C will also need MATH 20C or 31BH.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A and MATH 20B or 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20C or 31BH.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory—Mechanics
courses.description: Experiments include gravitational force, linear and rotational motion, conservation of energy and momentum, collisions, oscillations and springs, gyroscopes. Data reduction and error analysis are required for written laboratory reports. One hour lecture and three hours laboratory.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 2B or 4C.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Fluids, Waves, Thermodynamics, and Optics
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 2B covering fluid mechanics, waves in elastic media, sound waves, temperature, heat and the first law of thermodynamics, kinetic theory of gases, entropy and the second law of thermodynamics, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, geometric optics, interference and diffraction. Students continuing to PHYS 2D will need MATH 20D.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, and MATH 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20D. Prior completion of PHYS 2B is strongly recommended.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory—Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Experiments on L-R-C circuits; oscillations, resonance and damping, measurement of magnetic fields. One hour lecture and three hours laboratory. Program or materials fee may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, and 2B or 4C. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 2C or 4D.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Relativity and Quantum Physics
courses.description: A modern physics course covering atomic view of matter, electricity and radiation, atomic models of Rutherford and Bohr, relativity, X-rays, wave and particle duality, matter waves, Schrödinger’s equation, atomic view of solids, natural radioactivity.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, 2B, and MATH 20D. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20E.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics for Physics Majors—Fluids, Waves, Statistical and Thermal Physics
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 4A covering forced and damped oscillations, fluid statics and dynamics, waves in elastic media, sound waves, heat and the first law of thermodynamics, kinetic theory of gases, Brownian motion, Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, second law of thermodynamics. Students continuing to PHYS 4C will also need MATH 18 or 20F or 31AH.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A and MATH 20A-B. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20C or 31BH.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics for Physics Majors—Quantum Physics
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 4D covering experimental basis of quantum mechanics: Schrodinger equation and simple applications; spin; identical particles, Fermi and Bose distributions, density matrix, pure and mixed states, entangled states and EPR.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A-B-C-D or the combination of PHYS 4A and 4C and 4D and PHYS 2A-B-C, MATH 20A-B-C or 31BH, 20D, 20E or 31CH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Introductory Special Topics
courses.description: From time to time a member of the regular faculty or a resident visitor will give a self-contained course on an introductory topic in their special area of research or help students prepare to succeed in the physics major. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only. May be repeated up to six times, provided the same topic is not repeated.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetism III
courses.description: Electromagnetic waves, radiation theory; application to optics; motion of charged particles in electromagnetic fields; relation of electromagnetism to relativistic concepts.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 100B. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mathematical and Computational Physics II
courses.description: A continuation of PHYS 105A covering selected advanced topics in applied mathematical and numerical methods. Topics include statistics, diffusion and Monte-Carlo simulations; Laplace equation and numerical methods for nonseparable geometries; waves in inhomogeneous media, WKB analysis; nonlinear systems and chaos.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 105A, MATH 20A-B-C or 31BH, 20D, 20E or 31CH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Circuits and Electronics
courses.description: Laboratory and lecture course that covers principles of analog circuit theory and design, linear systems theory, and practical aspects of circuit realization, debugging, and characterization. Laboratory exercises include passive circuits, active filters and amplifiers with discrete and monolithic devices, nonlinear circuits, interfaces to sensors and actuators, and the digitization of analog signals. PHYS 120 was formerly numbered PHYS 120A. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A-B-C, and 2CL. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only. Recommended preparation: PHYS 100A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Physics I
courses.description: Development of quantum mechanics. Wave mechanics; measurement postulate and measurement problem. Piece-wise constant potentials, simple harmonic oscillator, central field and the hydrogen atom. Three hours lecture, one-hour discussion session.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A-B-C-D-E, 100A, 110A. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Physics II
courses.description: Matrix mechanics, angular momentum, spin, and the two-state system. Approximation methods and the hydrogen spectrum. Identical particles, atomic and nuclear structures. Scattering theory. Three hours lecture, one-hour discussion session.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 100B and 130A. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Statistical and Thermal Physics I
courses.description: Integrated treatment of thermodynamics and statistical mechanics; statistical treatment of entropy, review of elementary probability theory, canonical distribution, partition function, free energy, phase equilibrium, introduction to ideal quantum gases.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 130A. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Computational Physics I: Probabilistic Models and Simulations
courses.description: Project-based computational physics laboratory course with student’s choice of Fortran 90/95, or C/C++. Applications from materials science to the structure of the early universe are chosen from molecular dynamics, classical and quantum Monte Carlo methods, physical Langevin/Fokker-Planck processes.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electronic Materials
courses.description: Physics of electronic materials. Semiconductors: bands, donors and acceptors, devices. Metals: Fermi surface, screening, optical properties. Insulators: dia-/ferro-electrics, displacive transitions. Magnets: dia-/para-/ferro-/antiferro-magnetism, phase transitions, low temperature properties. Superconductors: pairing, Meissner effect, flux quantization, BCS theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 152A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Modern Cosmology
courses.description: An introduction to our current understanding of the universe, its history and content. The course introduces the geometry of the universe, the origin of structure, maps of the universe, and inference of cosmic parameters. Topics include big bang nucleosynthesis, the cosmic microwave background, the quantum origin of density fluctuations, dark matter, and the cosmological constant.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A-B-C-D-E.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantitative Microbiology
courses.description: A quantitative description of bacteria from molecular interactions through cellular and population level behaviors. Topics will vary yearly, covering process including gene regulation, molecular signaling, genetic circuits, stochastic dynamics, metabolic control, cell division, cell growth control, stress response, chemotaxis, biofilm formation. May be coscheduled with PHYS 276.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 140A. Recommended preparation: an introductory course in statistical mechanics or equivalent; ordinary differential equations.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics of the Cell
courses.description: Exploration of the physics problems that must be solved by a living cell in order to survive. Theoretical ideas from nonequilibrium statistical mechanics and dynamical systems are used to establish the physical principles that underlie biological function, focusing on the organization and behavior of eukaryotic cells. Specific topics rotate from year to year and may include genome organization and dynamics, motility, sensing, and organelle interaction. May be coscheduled with PHYS 277.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Recommended preparation: familiarity with statistical mechanics at the level of PHYS 140A or CHEM 132.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem by special arrangement with a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and departmental chair.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Honors Thesis Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Honors thesis research for seniors participating in the Honors Program. Research is conducted under the supervision of a physics faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Honors Program in Physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Advanced Classical Electrodynamics II
courses.description: Radiation from current distributions and accelerated charges, multipole radiation fields, waveguides and resonant cavities, electrodynamics of media.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 203A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Equilibrium Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Statistical ensembles: microcanonical, canonical, and grand canonical formulations; principle of maximum entropy. Thermodynamics: thermodynamic potentials, phase equilibria, entropy of mixing. Quantum statistics: photon statistics; ideal Bose and Fermi gases. Interacting systems: Ising model, liquids and plasmas. Phase transitions: van der Waals system, mean field theory, Landau theory, global symmetries, fluctuations.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 200A, 212A-B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics III
courses.description: Topics may include basics of many-body quantum mechanics, second quantization; basics of quantum information theory; path integrals, topological phases, and Aharonov-Bohm effect; stability of matter; atomic and molecular structure.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 212A-B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Fields III
courses.description: Aspects of gauge theories. Introduction to non-Abelian global and approximate symmetries. Introduction to non-Abelian gauge theories, including canonical and path integral quantization, perturbative calculations, asymptotic freedom. Spontaneous symmetry breaking. Selected additional topics including e.g., effective field theory, anomalies, instantons, monopoles, large N methods, lattice gauge theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 215A-B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Cosmology
courses.description: An advanced survey of topics in physical cosmology. The Friedmann models and the large-scale structure of the universe, including the observational determination of Ho (the Hubble constant) and qo (the deceleration parameter). Galaxy number counts. A systematic exposition of the physics of the early universe, including vacuum phase transitions; inflation; the generation of net baryon number, fluctuations, topological defects and textures. Primordial nucleosynthesis, both standard and nonstandard models. Growth and decay of adiabatic and isocurvature density fluctuations. Discussion of dark matter candidates and constraints from observation and experiment. Nucleocosmo-chronology and the determination of the age of the universe.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electronic Materials
courses.description: Physics of electronic materials. Semiconductors: bands, donors and acceptors, devices. Metals: Fermi surface, screening, optical properties. Insulators: dia-/ferro-electrics, displacive transitions. Magnets: dia-/para-/ferro-/antiferro-magnetism, phase transitions, low temperature properties. Superconductors: pairing, Meissner effect, flux quantization, BCS theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 211A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Computational Physics I: Probabilistic Models and Simulations
courses.description: Project-based computational physics laboratory course with student’s choice of Fortran90/95 or C/C++. Applications from materials science to the structure of the early universe are chosen from molecular dynamics, classical and quantum Monte Carlo methods, physical Langevin/Fokker-Planck processes, and other modern topics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussion of current research in physics of the solid state and of other condensed matter. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: High-Energy Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of current research in nuclear physics, principally in the field of elementary particles. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Plasma Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in plasma physics. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Astrophysics and Cosmology Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in astrophysics and cosmology. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biophysics Seminar
courses.description: Presentation of current research in biological physics and quantitative biology by invited speakers from the United States and abroad. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit thirty times.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biophysics Research Talks
courses.description: Discussion of recent research in biological physics and quantitative biology by current graduate students. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit thirty times.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Methods in Quantitative Biology
courses.description: Critical analysis of methods used to collect and analyze biological data. Topics include general aspects of experimental conditions for data collection and strategy of mathematical modeling, as well as specific methodologies in image acquisition, single cell analysis, population dynamics, and statistical data analysis. These topics will be covered through critical reading, peer discussion, problem solving on case studies selected by the instructors. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Colloquium
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in physics directed to the entire physics community. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantitative Microbiology
courses.description: A quantitative description of bacteria from molecular interactions through cellular and population level behaviors. Topics will vary yearly, covering processes including gene regulation, molecular signaling, genetic circuits, stochastic dynamics, metabolic control, cell division, cell growth control, stress response, chemotaxis, biofilm formation. May be coscheduled with PHYS 176. Recommended preparation: an introductory course in biology is helpful but not necessary.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics of the Cell
courses.description: Exploration of the physics problems that must be solved by a living cell in order to survive. Theoretical ideas from nonequilibrium statistical mechanics and dynamical systems are used to establish the physical principles that underlie biological function, focusing on the organization and behavior of eukaryotic cells. Specific topics rotate from year to year and may include genome organization and dynamics, motility, sensing, and organelle interaction. May be coscheduled with PHYS 177. The graduate version will include a report at the level of a research paper. Recommended preparation: familiarity with statistical mechanics at the level of PHYS 140A or CHEM 132.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Directed Study in Physics
courses.description: Research studies under the direction of a faculty member. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Thesis Research in Physics
courses.description: Directed research on dissertation topic. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The U.S. Congress
courses.description: This course will examine the nomination and election of congressmen, constituent relationships, the development of the institution, formal and informal structures, leadership, comparisons of House with Senate, lobbying, and relationship with the executive branch.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Data Analysis and United States Politics
courses.description: This course examines U.S. politics from a computational point of view. Through in-class work and hands-on assignments, we will use data analysis tools to collect, analyze, and visualize data related to various facets of federal level politics in the US. Students will develop statistical and computational skills that will assist them in advanced analyses of elections, legislative outcomes, lobbying, and other dynamics of the lawmaking process in Congress.
courses.prerequisites_text: POLI 5D/POLI 5D/ECON 5 or POLI 30D.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Revolution and Reaction: Political Thought from Kant to Nietzsche
courses.description: The course deals with the period that marks the triumph and critique of the modern state. Central topics include the development of the idea of class, of the irrational, of the unconscious, and of rationalized authority as they affect politics. Readings drawn from Rousseau, Kant, Hegel, Marx, Nietzsche, and others.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Theory
courses.description: An undergraduate course designed to cover various aspects of political theory. May be repeated for credit two times, provided each course is a separate topic, for a maximum of twelve units.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Germany: Before, During, and After Division
courses.description: Consideration of political, economic, and security factors that have kept Germany at the center of European developments for more than a century.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: European Integration
courses.description: This course reviews the origins and development of the European Community/European Union and its institutions, theories of integration and the challenges inherent in the creation of a supranational political regime.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Comparative LGBT Politics
courses.description: This course is designed to expose students to the study of LGBT politics, focusing specifically on the formation of LGBT movements, the presence (or absence) of political opportunities to advance their desired goals, as well as their political success (or lack thereof). Although the course will initially examine the U.S. LGBT movement, the course will also examine the formation (and political success/failure) of LGBT movements in other democratic political systems.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Human Rights Law: Migrant Populations
courses.description: International migration creates a distinct set of human rights challenges. This course examines the conflict between international legal obligations and domestic politics of citizenship, human rights, asylum, and human trafficking.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Spies, Intelligence, and U.S. National Security
courses.description: Information is the key to success and failure in U.S. foreign policy. This course will cover the American intelligence community’s secret and information gathering processes. The curriculum is organized by the specialist functions of real-world IC professionals. You will learn methods for collecting raw data, including human and signals intelligence, how that data is synthesized into intelligence, the different reporting formats that drive national security decisions, and about oversight and ethical issues.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics of Immigration
courses.description: Comparative analysis of attempts by the United States and other industrialized countries to initiate, regulate and reduce immigration from Third World countries. Social and economic factors shaping outcomes of immigration policies, public opinion toward immigrants, anti-immigration movements, and immigration policy reform options in industrialized countries.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing required.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to Policy Analysis
courses.description: (Same as USP 101) This course will explore the process by which the preferences of individuals are converted into public policy. Also included will be an examination of the complexity of policy problems, methods for designing better policies, and a review of tools used by analysts and policy makers.
courses.prerequisites_text: POLI 10 or 11.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Making Policy with Data
courses.description: This class explores how we can make policy recommendations using data. We attempt to establish causal relationships between policy intervention and outcomes based on statistical evidence. Hands-on examples will be provided throughout the course.
courses.prerequisites_text: POLI 5 or 5D or ECON 5 and POLI 30 or 30D.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Social Network Analysis
courses.description: This class introduces tools for analyzing social networks including graph visualization, egocentric and sociocentric network measures, network simulation, and data management.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Machine Learning for Social Scientists
courses.description: This course focuses on statistical and algorithmic techniques to analyze and utilize large collections of data for social science inferences. The goal of the course is to introduce students to modern machine learning methods and provide the skills necessary to apply the methods widely. In achieving this goal, students will learn about core concepts in machine learning and statistics, developing skills that are transferable to other types of data and inference problems.
courses.prerequisites_text: CCS 1 or ECON 5/5R or POLI 5/5D/5R/5DR or POLI 30/30D.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Research Seminar in Washington, DC
courses.description: (Same as COMM 194, USP 194, HITO 193, SOCI 194, COGS 194) Course attached to six-unit internship taken by students participating in the UCDC Program. Involves weekly seminar meetings with faculty and teaching assistant and a substantial research paper.
courses.prerequisites_text: participating in UCDC Program.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Local Internship Research Seminar
courses.description: The Local Internship Research Seminar will be paired with a Local Internship in Political Science (POLI 197SD) in the same quarter. The linkage to this research seminar will provide advanced academic training in analytic skills appropriate to the internship experience and requires a substantial paper based on original research.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval and consent of instructor. Corequisites: POLI 197SD.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Local Internship in Political Science
courses.description: Individual placements for field learning integrated with political science. A written contract involving all parties with learning objectives, a project outline, and a means of supervision and progress evaluation must be filed with the faculty adviser and department undergraduate coordinator prior to the beginning of the internship. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: ninety units completed; 2.5 minimum cumulative GPA overall and 3.0 in political science; POLI 30 and at least two upper-division courses in political science. Department approval and consent of instructor. Corequisites: POLI 194SD.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Research Apprenticeship
courses.description: Students conduct directed research as part of a principal investigator’s project and under the supervision of a department mentor. Students may conduct research with a department mentor for up to two quarters. This course is part of the Research Apprenticeship program in political science. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval. Students must apply for the Research Apprenticeship program and be approved to enroll. Participants must be majors in political science with junior or senior standing and a GPA of 3.5 or higher in all political science courses taken at UC San Diego. Individual projects may require other prerequisite training, such as POLI 30.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading in advanced political science by individual students. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Analytic Theory II
courses.description: The second in the two-course sequence on the essentials of game theory and fundamental concepts in the social sciences. This course introduces multistage and repeated games, as well as static and dynamic games with incomplete information. Applications include axiomatic and strategic models of negotiations, bargaining in legislatures, auctions, adverse selection problems, market failures, signaling and screening, reputation, conventions, and cheap talk.
courses.prerequisites_text: POLI 203A, graduate student standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Contemporary Sociological Theory
courses.description: (Same as Soc/G 202.) Themes important for social theory at the turn of the twenty-first century: Marxism, Gramsci, Althusser, critical theory (Adorno, Habermas), interpretation (Geertz), social systems (Parson), poststructuralism (Foucault), postmodernism, and social constructivism (Bourdieu).
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Marxist and Post-Marxist Political Philosophy
courses.description: An examination of selected texts in Marxist and post-Marxist political philosophy, with a focus on the theme of individual and collective identity including issues concerning alienation, consciousness, and ideology.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Security
courses.description: A colloquium surveying the major theoretical controversies in the study of international and national security.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Political Economy
courses.description: A seminar surveying the major theoretical controversies in the study of international political economy.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Politics of Race, Ethnicity, and Immigration
courses.description: This course examines the interplay between racial/ethnic identity and politics. How do race and ethnicity become politicized? What role does ethnic or racial identity play in political behavior and decision-making processes? To what extent do political institutions and institutional design reinforce the salience of ethnic or racial identity in politics? We will be taking a comparative approach to this topic, and cover readings in both American politics and comparative politics literature.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race, Class, and Institutions in American Political Economy
courses.description: This course will explore how institutions address and/or perpetuate racial, ethnic, and economic inequality in the US.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Causal Inference
courses.description: This course covers designs and methods of causal inference, including randomized experiments, cross-sectional and longitudinal designs, and other tools such as sensitivity analysis and randomization inference. These methods are illustrated with examples in political science and positive political economy.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: International Law and Regulation
courses.description: Examination of recent research in international law and regulation: development and presentation of research projects by graduate students; presentation of research by faculty. Third-year students present dissertation prospectus, candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit three times as topics vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: American Politics
courses.description: Examination of recent research in American politics: development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentations of research by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: Comparative Politics
courses.description: Examination of recent research in comparative politics, development and presentation of research projects by graduate students; presentations of research projects by faculty. Third-year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: International Relations
courses.description: Examination of recent research in international relations, development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentations of research projects by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentation of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: Political Theory
courses.description: Examination of recent research in political theory: development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentation of research by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: Methodology
courses.description: Examination of recent research in political methodology; development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentation of research by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Directed Reading
courses.description: Guided and supervised reading in the literature of the several fields of political science.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.description: Independent work by graduate students engaged in research and writing of second-year paper and doctoral dissertation, under direct supervision of adviser.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the basic concepts in psychology. Topics may include human information processing, learning and memory, motivation, development, language acquisition, social psychology, and personality.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology: Cognitive Foundations
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the basic concepts of cognitive psychology. Topics include perception, attention, memory, language, and thought. The relation of cognitive psychology to cognitive science and to neuropsychology is also covered.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology: Developmental Foundations
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to theories and research results in developmental psychology, covering infancy through adulthood.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Introduction to Statistics
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to both descriptive and inferential statistics, core tools in the process of scientific discovery and the interpretation of research.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of how to choose appropriate research methods for experimental and nonexperimental studies. Topics may include classic experimental design and counterbalancing, statistical power, and causal inference in experimental and nonexperimental settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 60 or equivalent.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Laboratory in Psychological Research Methods
courses.description: This course provides hands-on research experience. Lecture topics will include experimental and nonexperimental designs, research ethics, data analysis, and causal inference. Students will design original research projects, collect and analyze data, and write a full APA-style report, including a brief literature review relevant to their design. This course builds on PSYC 70 by applying design principles to students’ own research questions and ideas. Open to the following Department of Psychology majors only: PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, COGS 14B or PSYC 60 or MATH 11 and PSYC 70 or COGS 14A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Learning Sustainable Well-Being: Compassion for Self and Others
courses.description: This experiential course teaches the art of practicing psychological well-being based on principles from Eastern and Western philosophies (e.g., mindfulness, positive psychology, cognitive therapy, and neuroscience). Each week, there is a short lecture on a given topic, combined with workshop-style exercises.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or research under direction of a member of the faculty. May be taken up to three times for a maximum of twelve units.
courses.prerequisites_text: lower-division standing, completion of at least thirty units of undergraduate study at UC San Diego with a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0; completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Clinical Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the causes, characteristics, and treatment of psychological disorders. Particular emphasis is given to the interaction between biological, psychological, and sociocultural processes contributing to abnormal behavior. Students may not receive credit for both PSYC 163 and PSYC 100.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the field of developmental psychology, including topics in cognitive, language, and social development.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Sensory Neuroscience
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the neural mechanisms that support vision, audition, touch, olfaction, and taste.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the field of social psychology, covering a review of the field’s founding principles, classic findings, and a survey of recent findings. Topics will include social perception, attributions and attitudes, stereotypies, social influence, group dynamics, and aggressive and prosocial tendencies.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of cognitive psychology, the scientific study of mental processes: how people acquire, store, transform, use, and communicate information. Topics may include perception, attention, language, memory, reasoning, problem solving, decision-making, and creativity.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of human and animal behavior from a neuroscience perspective. Topics include the functions and mechanisms of perception, motivation (sex, sleep, hunger, emotions), learning and memory, and motor control and movement.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Methods II
courses.description: This course builds upon the material of PSYC 111A. Students will participate in data collection, data organization, statistical analysis and graphical analysis, with emphasis placed on developing scientific report writing, presentations, and critical thinking about experimental methods. Must be taken for a letter grade for the Psychology Honors Program.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 111A; upper-division standing. Instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Health Sciences Research
courses.description: In this course, students explore major models in mental health research and apply them in laboratory settings, examining how team science generates knowledge and influences society. Through literature review and focused discussions on study design, methodology, and research ethics, they develop skills in critical analysis and proposal writing. If interested, students with satisfactory performance may continue research with the PI for academic credit by pursuing PSYC 199 in health sciences.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Laboratory in Animal Behavior
courses.description: This course provides an opportunity to learn about the various evolutionary forces that shape a species’ natural behavioral repertoire while also conducting research related to these issues. Classroom lectures on topics related to ethology will be complemented by a research project in which students collect observational data on animal behavior. Open to the following majors only: PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, CG32.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, PSYC 60 or COGS 14B or MATH 11 and PSYC 70 or COGS 14A, and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Sexual Health Inequities and Sexual Well-Being
courses.description: This course provides an overview of sexual health inequities and sexual well-being. Students will engage critically and reflexively in topics related to race/ethnicity, gender, and sexual orientation. Open to the following Department of Psychology majors only: PC25, PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, PC35.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, PSYC 60, PSYC 70, PSYC 172.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Hormones and Behavior
courses.description: This course examines how hormones influence a variety of behaviors and how behavior reciprocally influences hormones. Specific topics covered include aggression, sex and sexuality, feeding, learning, memory, mood and neural mechanisms both in humans and nonhuman animals. Recommended preparation: completion of PSYC 106.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Belief in Weird Things
courses.description: Why do people think that the Earth is flat or that knocking on wood wards off bad luck? False beliefs emerge as byproducts of an otherwise efficient cognitive system. In this course, you will explore how people come to believe in myths, fake news, conspiracy theories, superstitions, astrology, alternative medicine, and alien life. You will learn to use skeptical and scientific thinking to evaluate “weird” (and not so weird) claims.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Cognition
courses.description: This course provides an overview of social cognition, which blends cognitive and social psychology to understand how people make sense of the social world. Topics may include social perception, inference, memory, motivation, affect, understanding the self, stereotypes, and cultural cognition.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Memory and Amnesia
courses.description: This course will provide a survey of current research and theory concerning human memory and amnesia from both cognitive and neuropsychological perspectives. Topics may include short-term (working) memory, encoding and retrieval, episodic and semantic memory, interference and forgetting, false memory, eyewitness memory, emotion and memory, famous case studies of amnesia, and the effects of aging and dementia on memory.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Language
courses.description: This course provides an overview of language comprehension and production. Topics include animal communication, language development, and language disorders. Recommended preparation: completion of a course in language, cognition, or philosophy of the mind.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Neuroscience of Decision-Making
courses.description: This topics course provides an overview on the neurobiology of decision-making; covering topics related to the neurobiology of decision-making. The goal of this class is twofold: explore how the brain does decision-making and its disruption in disease states, and build know-how and experience in reading and discussing primary research papers.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; PSYC 106.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Criminology
courses.description: This course provides the classic and new disciplinary paradigms explaining criminal behavior using developmental, environmental, cultural, social, and personality theory perspectives and methods. The course will include different manifestations of crime (e.g., violent, white-collar, organized) and the influences of criminal justice responses (punishment, rehabilitation, recidivism, etc.).
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
courses.description: This course provides an overview of human sexuality research including diversity of sexual behavior and identities, sex and gender development, intimate relationships, and sexual dysfunction. Recommended preparation: completion of PSYC 1, 2, or 106.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Industrial Organizational Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an examination of human behavior in industrial, business, and organizational settings. Topics include psychological principles applied to selection, placement, management, and training; the effectiveness of individuals and groups within organizations, including leadership and control; conflict and cooperation; motivation; and organizational structure and design.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Drugs, Addiction, and Mental Disorders
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the use, abuse, liability, and psychotherapeutic effects of drugs on humans.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Climate Crisis
courses.description: This course provides tools for the student to think about the escalating climate crisis. Urgent action is needed at a large, societal scale to prevent the worst consequences of anthropogenic global heating. Better understanding the prospects for such action can come from human psychology. How do people arrive at their beliefs? What is the basis of denial and delay? How does belief flow to action? What kinds of actions can people take?
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Impulse Control Disorders
courses.description: This course provides an overview of problems of impulse control, which are important features of major psychiatric disorders and also of atypical patterns of behavior including pathological gambling, compulsive sex, eating, exercise, and shopping. Topics include development, major common features, treatment, and neurobiological basis of impulse control disorders.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Science of Parenting
courses.description: This course provides an interdisciplinary overview of theories and scientific research on parenting. Topics may include family structure, parenting styles, attachment, discipline strategies, culture, and media. This course also takes a critical approach to the scientific evidence regarding the role of parents in child development. Topics may include behavior genetics, discipline, diet, sleep, the nature of learning, screen time, impulse control, and vaccination.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Topics in Psychology
courses.description: Selected topics in the field of psychology. May be taken for credit three times as topics vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology Laboratory Topics
courses.description: Selected laboratory topics in the field of psychology. May be taken for credit two times as topics vary. Open to the following majors only: PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, CG32.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, department approval, and PSYC 60 or COGS 14B or MATH 11 and PSYC 70 or COGS 14A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Honors Thesis III
courses.description: This course provides the opportunity for students to complete their research, write their honors thesis, and present their results at the Honors Poster Session. Must be taken for a letter grade for the Psychology Honors Program.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 194A-B, department approval, psychology majors only, acceptance to the Honors program.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Weekly research seminar, three quarter research project under faculty guidance which culminates in a thesis. Must be taken for a letter grade to satisfy major requirements for Department of Psychology majors. Open to the following majors only: PC25, PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, PC35.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Directed Group Study in Psychology
courses.description: Group study under the direction of a faculty member in the Department of Psychology.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or laboratory research under direction of faculty in the Department of Psychology. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Cognitive Neural Systems (CNS)
courses.description: A weekly seminar series focused on understanding recent advances in the relationship between neural systems and behavior using a variety of experimental approaches (single unit recording, comp neuro, evolutionary bio, psychophysics, comparative anatomy, lesion work, psychopharm, fMRI, EEG, TMS, etc.). May be taken for credit twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Advanced seminar concentrating on methods of research and current experimental literature in developmental psychology. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Introduction to Laboratory Experimentation III
courses.description: Final quarter of basic laboratory course designed to introduce first-year graduate students to experimental methods in psychology. The student will select a research topic; do a thorough literature review of the area; design and carry out new, original studies of problems in the selected area; and prepare a final formal report of the study at the end of the spring quarter. This course is required of all first-year graduate students in the department. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Selected Topics in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of selected empirical and theoretical topics in cognitive psychology. The course will focus on areas where notable progress appears to be taking place in contemporary research.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Social Psychology
courses.description: A biweekly seminar series focusing on recent advances in both basic and applied research in social psychology including topics such as interpersonal relationships, emotion, health, social cognition, judgment, and decision making. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: A weekly seminar series focused on understanding recent advances in any area of cognitive psychology. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Selected Topics in Social Psychology
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of selected empirical and theoretical topics in social psychology. The course will focus on areas where notable progress appears to be taking place in contemporary research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Seminar in Communication and Information Processing
courses.description: S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: Research in psychology under supervision of individual faculty members. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit fifteen times.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: Independent research and thesis research. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit fifteen times.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: Teaching practicum for students enrolled in graduate program in psychology. Students who hold appointments as teaching assistants must enroll in this course. Minimum program requirement is for one four-unit course per year for four years. S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Methods and Ethics in Public Health Research
courses.description: This course will lay a foundation for understanding how to conduct research to answer questions about public health. It aims to teach students why research is done the way it is, what questions we can and can’t answer, and the methodological and ethical limits that must be considered along the way. Students will learn to think critically about the implications and limitations of existing research, and to form their own research questions about public health and the ways to investigate answers.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Primary Care and Public Health
courses.description: This course explores historical and current interactions, achievements, and challenges of primary care and public health. It will analyze the impact of common medical conditions such as obesity, diabetes, mental health disorders, and others on individuals, their families, and society. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 50. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 50 and PH 50.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Learning Sustainable Well-Being: Compassion for Self and Others, a Public Health Perspective
courses.description: This experiential course teaches the art of practicing psychological well-being, based on Eastern and Western approaches (e.g., mindfulness, positive psychology, cognitive therapy, neuroscience, theatre and art), from the perspective of public health. Each week there is a short lecture on a given topic, combined with workshop-style exercises. This course is part of the Learning Sustainable Well-being Program. Visit lsw.ucsd.edu for more information.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Selected topics in the field of public health.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Investigation of public health topics through directed reading and discussion by a small group of students under supervision of a faculty member. Opportunities can also include experiential and research components. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: completion of thirty units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual undergraduate study or research not covered by the present course offerings. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: completion of thirty units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Epidemiology
courses.description: This course covers the basic principles of epidemiology, with applications to investigations of noninfectious (“chronic”) and infectious diseases. Explores various study designs appropriate for disease surveillance and studies of etiology and prevention. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 101. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 101 and PH 101.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PSYC 60, HDS 60, MATH 11, or COGS 14B, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Biostatistics in Public Health
courses.description: Fundamentals of biostatistics and basic methods for analysis of continuous and binary outcomes for one, two, or several groups. Includes: summarizing and displaying data; probability; statistical distributions; central limit theorem, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing; comparing means of continuous variables between two groups; comparing proportions between two groups; simple and multiple linear regression. Hands-on data analysis using software and statistical applications in public health. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 102. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 102 and PH 102.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PSYC 60, HDS 60, MATH 11, or COGS 14B, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Health Behavior and Chronic Diseases
courses.description: This course introduces health behavior concepts through applications to chronic disease prevention. The focus is on smoking, dietary behaviors, and physical activity and is organized around relationships to health, measurement, influencing factors, interventions, and translation to public health practice. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 110. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 110 and PH 110.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Health Policies for Healthy Lifestyles
courses.description: This course covers the rationale for and effectiveness of policies to influence nutrition, physical activity, and substance use behavior. Policies include legalization, taxation, labeling, produce manufacturing, warning labels, licensing, marketing, and counter-marketing practices and restrictions on use. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 120. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 120 and PH 120.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Environmental and Occupational Health
courses.description: This core public health course addresses the fundamentals of environmental and occupational health, including identification of hazards, basic toxicology, risk assessment, prevention/protection, and regulatory/control policies. Specific environmental and occupational hazards and relevant case studies will be presented. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 130. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 130 and PH 130.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 101 or FMPH 101, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Qualitative Research for Global Public Health
courses.description: An overview of the role of qualitative research methods in public health. The course will focus on qualitative research as it relates to formative program design, community-based participatory approaches, and as a tool for amplifying voices and elucidating both complex social-ecological processes and internal individual experiences. Throughout the term, students will work in teams to design, conduct, analyze, and report a full qualitative study on a public health topic of their choosing. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing. Renumbered from FMPH 155. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 155 and PH 155.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Critical Digital Health
courses.description: This course aims to empower students to critically evaluate digital consumer technologies related to health by exploring the social, cultural, and political contexts in which they are designed and used. Students will learn how to evaluate digital consumer tools that are and can be used by the public to promote health and will investigate both the benefits and the unintended consequences of digital health, and the ways in which it can reinforce marginalization.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and sophomore standing. Renumbered from FMPH 191. Students cannot receive credit for FMPH 162 if they have already completed FMPH 191 subtitled “Critical Digital Health.”

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Field Epidemiology and Outbreak Investigations
courses.description: This course consists of a series of practical epidemiological infectious and non-infectious disease paper- and computer-based exercises. Students will have the opportunity to apply their epidemiological and biostatistical skills to real-world situations. The course is highly interactive and challenges students’ knowledge and critical thinking capacities. Students will give presentations, write a scientific abstract and press release, and develop a poster. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PH 101 or FMPH 101. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing. Renumbered from FMPH 171. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 171 and PH 171.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Selected topics in the field of public health. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Additional prerequisites may be required at instructor’s discretion. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing. Department approval required. Renumbered from FMPH 191.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Capstone II
courses.description: This is the second of a two-part capstone series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students will interpret and contextualize findings from their projects completed in the first part of the series. Oral and written presentations will focus on disseminating public health information in diverse formats. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, PH 120 or FMPH 120, and PH 193 or FMPH 193. Department approval required. Restricted to senior public health majors only. Renumbered from FMPH 194. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: PH 194, PH 194R, or FMPH 194.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Pedagogy and Learning Apprenticeship
courses.description: Under the supervision of an instructor, undergraduate students gain teaching experience through practical experiences in course management and effective teaching methods. May be taken for credit up to two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: a minimum of A– in the course in which the student plans to assist, a 3.0 cumulative UC GPA, and instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Honors Practicum II
courses.description: This is the second of an accelerated two-part honors series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health majors. Students will analyze, interpret, and contextualize findings from their projects completed in the series. Oral and written communication will focus on disseminating public health information in diverse formats, and will include a presentation and an honors thesis. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 196AH. Department approval required. Restricted to upper-division public health majors only.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Investigation of public health topics through directed reading and discussion by a small group of students. Opportunities can also include experiential and research components. Study must be under supervision of a faculty member and approval must be secured from the faculty member prior to registering. P/NP grades only. Renumbered from FMPH 198. PH 198 and/or FMPH 198 may be taken for credit a combined total of nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual undergraduate study or research not covered by the present course offerings. Study or research must be under the direction of a faculty member in the Department of Family Medicine and Public Health and approval must be secured from the faculty member prior to registering. P/NP grades only. Renumbered from FMPH 199. PH 199 and/or FMPH 199 may be taken for credit a combined total of nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Advanced Methods in Health Services A
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to causal inference methodologies essential for empirical research in public health. Students will explore the distinctions between association and causation, the impacts of biases, and the role of randomized experiments and assignment mechanisms. Students will develop the skills to evaluate research designs and implement appropriate statistical techniques to identify and estimate causal relationships in both observational and experimental data.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Advanced Methods in Implementation Science
courses.description: This course examines the use of innovative methods that have been designed or tailored for use in monitoring, evaluating, and facilitating implementation of evidence-based programs, policies, and practices.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Epidemiology of Aging
courses.description: This course encompasses a range of topics related to aging including the demography of aging, hallmarks of biological aging, physiological reserve and resilience, physical and cognitive function, major chronic diseases of aging (diabetes, kidney disease, heart disease, cancer, osteoporosis, fracture, Alzheimer’s disease, and related dementias), multimorbidity, and epidemiology of healthy aging.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Epidemiology of Aging Lab
courses.description: The objectives of the epidemiology of aging lab supplement are to familiarize students with aging cohorts, prominent biases, and methodological approaches to addressing them; commonly used statistical methods; and common areas of epidemiological research in aging populations.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Grant Writing for Public Health
courses.description: Students will review funded and nonfunded grant proposals for different types of NIH awards, with an emphasis on R01 research awards. Students will have an opportunity to have their own proposals reviewed by instructors and classmates. The instructor will prepare a research proposal with help from the students.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Genetic Epidemiology
courses.description: The course introduces the fundamental concepts, principles, and methods in genetic epidemiology. The course reviews terminology used in genetics, introduces principles of population and human genetics, and provides an overview of the use of molecular and genetic methods in utilized genetic epidemiologic and clinical research. This includes the study designs used to identify the genetic basis of Mendelian and complex traits and diseases.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: HSRIS Colloquium Series
courses.description: The HSRIS colloquium series is a program of empirical research seminars focused on the most important issues facing patients, providers, health care systems, and policymakers today. It provides an opportunity for HSRIS doctoral students across all stages of completion to meet regularly, analyze and critique ongoing research, and participate in stimulating discussion with HSRIS faculty and guest lecturers.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Scale Development for Behavioral Health Measurement
courses.description: Course will present theory and methods for developing scales to assess public health-related constructs (e.g., physical, mental, and social well-being).

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Topics of special interest in public health. Topics may vary from quarter to quarter.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study in Public Health
courses.description: Individual graduate study or research not covered by present course offerings. Study or research must be under the direction of a faculty member in the School of Public Health and approval must be secured from the faculty member and track director prior to registering.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Dissertation Research in Public Health
courses.description: Public health doctoral program dissertation research units.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Research Methods
courses.description: This course will focus on fundamental concepts in research design and measurement to understand methodological considerations in quantitative and qualitative scientific studies in public health and be able to critically evaluate public health research. Emphasis will be on creating testable hypotheses, designing a hypothetical study to test the hypothesis, and assessing methods of measurement.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 403. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 403 and PH 403.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Occupational Health
courses.description: This course examines the relationship between human activities, the environment, and health. It explores how environments affect well-being, focusing on hazards from workplaces and contamination. It also addresses personal and societal behaviors impacting environmental health and reviews strategies to mitigate negative human effects at individual and community levels.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 404. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 404 and PH 404.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Health Behavior Interventions
courses.description: This course focuses on critical analyses of health behavior theories and their applications to interventions in multiple fields, such as (but not limited to) nutrition, cancer, and physical activity. The course will prepare students to design, plan, implement, and evaluate health behavior interventions covering individual and population approaches to behavior change.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB87) or program approval and successfully completed PH 402. Renumbered from FMPH 410. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 410 and PH 410.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Infectious Diseases and Public Health
courses.description: Designed to increase understanding of the history, classification, surveillance, prevention, and control of major and emerging infectious diseases. Lectures, assignments, and discussions will also introduce students to methods of particular relevance to infectious disease epidemiology.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401. Renumbered from FMPH 418. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 418 and PH 418.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Mental and Behavior Health and Addiction
courses.description: This course introduces key aspects of mental and behavioral health as well as the etiology, risk factors, and impact of mental disorders in public health. The focus will be given to the link between mental and physical health and the impact of mental health on health behavior and outcomes. Mental and behavioral health in relation to substance use and addiction will be covered. Intervention strategies to improve mental and behavioral health will be introduced.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, and PB89) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 402 or PH 402. Renumbered from FMPH 402. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 402 and PH 402.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Technology and Precision Health
courses.description: This course will introduce students to the field of precision health and will provide a broad overview of a variety of emerging technologies (artificial intelligence, informatics, big data and data science, genomics, spatial data, digital health, predictive analytics). Students will be prompted to consider the applications to public health policy and practice.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB90) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 430. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 430 and PH 430.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Health Economics
courses.description: This course will introduce key concepts in health economics and apply these concepts to better understand and evaluate health policy issues in the U.S. health-care system. It will also introduce basic microeconomic analysis tools from the perspective of public health. Module 1 gives an overview of the U.S. health-care system and introduces microeconomic tools. Module 2 examines key players in the U.S. health-care system. Module 3 introduces economic evaluation tools and health policy issues.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB88) and successfully completed FMPH 405 or PH 405. Renumbered from FMPH 440. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 440 and PH 440.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: VIIDAI: Public Health Field Practice in Baja
courses.description: Students will develop an understanding of field epidemiology, surveillance, survey development, data collection, analysis, and presentation. They may also be exposed to planning, implementing, and evaluating age- and culturally-appropriate health promotion interventions. They will learn about cultural awareness, international travel safety, gain collaborative group experience with other institutions to carry out duties that will be put into practice during the class field trip.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91). Students cannot receive credit for PH 463 if they have already completed FMPH 491 subtitled “VIIDAI: Public Health Field Practice in Baja.”

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Foundation and Government Grant Writing (Non-NIH)
courses.description: Students learn the skill of grant writing as used by academics, practitioners, and leaders of the public health community to support program development and implementation, technical assistance and capacity building, resource development, research projects, training programs, and other areas. Students will learn strategies for successful teamwork and be introduced to strategies to identify and respond to grant opportunities using a data-driven and theoretically sound approach.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91).

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
