courses.description: Each student enrolled will be required to write an honors essay, a substantial research paper on a current urban policy issue, under the supervision of a member of the faculty. Most often the essay will be based on their previous fieldwork courses and internship. This essay and other written exercises, as well as class participation, will be the basis of the final grade for the course. The seminar will rotate from year to year among the faculty in urban studies and planning.
courses.prerequisites_text: USP 187 or USP 185B, major GPA 3.5, and department approval. This is an application-based course.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Advanced GIS for Urban and Community Planning
courses.description: Advanced geographic information systems (GIS) as applied to urban studies. Learn to use the GIS software with a focus on data management, online GIS, elements of spatial statistics, technologies, and models for spatial data integration to support urban research and decision-making.
courses.prerequisites_text: USP 191A and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: San Diego Community Research
courses.description: Using the San Diego region as a case study, students will be introduced to the process of collecting, evaluating, and presenting urban and regional data using a variety of methods, including aggregate data analysis, historical research, and ethnography.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Research Seminar in Washington, DC
courses.description: (Same as COGS 194, COMM 194, HITO 193, POLI 194, SOCI 194, SIO 194.) Course attached to six-unit internship taken by students participating in the UCDC Program. Involves weekly seminar meetings with faculty and teaching assistant and a substantial research paper.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval and participating in UCDC Program.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Pedagogy and Learning Apprenticeship
courses.description: Under the supervision of an instructor, undergraduate students gain teaching experience through practical experiences in course management and effective teaching methods. May be taken for credit up to three times for a maximum of eight units.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study on a topic or in a field not included in the regular departmental curriculum by special arrangement with a faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Reading and research programs and field-study projects to be arranged between student and instructor, depending on the student’s needs and the instructor’s advice in terms of these needs.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to Art Making: Three-Dimensional Practices
courses.description: An idea-driven introduction to contemporary art practice, covering three-dimensional work relating to transformation, representation, workmanship, design, movement, time, and context. Students are asked to think openly and critically about art, and to articulate their ideas in physical form using various materials and products. This course is offered only one time each year.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Computing in the Arts Lecture Series
courses.description: Designed around presentations by visiting artists, critics, and scientists involved with contemporary issues related to computer arts and design. Lectures by the instructor and contextual readings provide background material for the visitor presentations. Program or materials fees may apply. Students may not receive credit for both VIS 10 and ICAM 110. This course is offered only one time each year.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to the Art of the Americas or Africa and Oceania
courses.description: Course offers a comparative and thematic approach to the artistic achievements of societies with widely divergent structures and political organizations from the ancient Americas to Africa and the Pacific Islands. Topics vary with the interests and expertise of instructor. Students may not receive credit for VIS 21 and VIS 21A.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Formations of Modern Art
courses.description: A wide-ranging survey introducing the key aspects of global art and criticism in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The course will comparatively examine formations of modernism and modernity within and across a variety of aesthetic traditions in Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, North America, and Oceania. This course is a distance education course. Students may not receive credit for both VIS 22 and VIS 22R.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Art, Design, and the Brain
courses.description: Neuroscience is a fast-growing biology field, with projects such as the White House BRAIN Initiative and the Allen Brain Atlas and new areas such as neuroeconomics, neurophilosophy, and neuroaesthetics. This lecture course considers interactions between neuroscience and art, primarily focusing on studies of how art is represented in the brain. By considering perception, emotion, memory, and creativity, we approach scientific understandings of art and design.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Design Communication
courses.description: This course provides a strong foundation in contemporary techniques of design communication, introduced in light of their significance to visual culture and the speculative design field. We cover digital image editing, typography, vector-based illustration and diagramming, and document layout. Also introduced are basic digital video editing tools and web production formats. Emphasis is on mastery of craft through iteration and presentation of multiple projects.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to Digital Photography
courses.description: An in-depth exploration of the camera and image utilizing photographic digital technology. Emphasis is placed on developing fundamental control of the processes and materials through lectures, field, and lab experience. Basic discussion of image making included. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. Open to visual arts majors and minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to Media
courses.description: Operating as both a lecture and production course, this introductory class provides a technical foundation and theoretical context for all subsequent production-oriented film and video studies. In the laboratory, the student will learn the basic skills necessary to initiate video production. Completion of Visual Arts 70N is necessary to obtain a media card. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. Open to visual arts and cinematic arts majors and minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Film History
courses.description: A survey of the history and the art of the cinema. The course will cover a range of national and international cinemas from the origins of cinema and the contributions of the earliest filmmakers to film movements and styles of the late twentieth century. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Designing Urban Ecologies
courses.description: This course will explore and develop designs and strategies that use multi-scalar urban and ecological systems as materials for artistic intervention and design speculation on structures including shifting geopolitical boundaries, sociocultural territories, and urban infrastructures and landscapes. Through hands-on research and design projects, we explore the city and its multiple sites of investigation to develop new ecologies of social and cultural productions.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 101.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Democratizing the City
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the Tijuana-San Diego border, seeing it as a microcosm of global conflict from where to engage urban inequality and explore new approaches to democratize the city. The course zooms into the border flows that make the marginalized neighborhoods within this contested geography into sites of social-economic and cultural productivity, laboratories in which to rethink the gap between wealth and poverty.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Drawing: Representing the Subject
courses.description: A studio course in beginning drawing covering basic drawing and composition. These concepts will be introduced by the use of models, still life, landscapes, and conceptual projects.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 80.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Drawing: Practices and Genre
courses.description: A continuation of VIS 105A. A studio course in which the student will investigate a wider variety of technical and conceptual issues involved in contemporary art practice related to drawing.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 105A.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Painting: Image Making
courses.description: A studio course focusing on problems inherent in painting—transferring information and ideas onto a two-dimensional surface, color, composition, as well as manual and technical procedures. These concepts will be explored through the use of models, still life, and landscapes.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 80.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Painting: Practices and Genre
courses.description: A continuation of VIS 106A. A studio course in which the student will investigate a wider variety of technical and conceptual issues involved in contemporary art practice related to painting.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 106A.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Painting: Portfolio Projects
courses.description: A studio course in painting emphasizing individual creative problems. Class projects, discussions, and critiques will focus on issues related to intention, subject matter, and context.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 106B.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Sculpture: Making the Object
courses.description: A studio course focusing on the problems involved in transferring ideas and information into three-dimensions. Course will explore materials and construction as dictated by the intended object. Specific problems to be investigated will be determined by the individual professor.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 80.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Sculpture: Practices and Genre
courses.description: A studio course in which the student will investigate a wider variety of technical and conceptual issues as well as materials involved in contemporary art practice related to sculpture.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 107A.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Advanced Projects in Art
courses.description: This is a studio art course for the advanced visual arts major. After guided assignments, emphasis is on self-directed projects and portfolio development. This interdisciplinary course may focus on painting, drawing, sculpture, performance, film, video, photography, and new media. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: senior standing. Open to media, studio, ICAM, and speculative design majors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Visual Narrative
courses.description: This course for the advanced visual arts major explores the role of storytelling in art practice across a variety of disciplines including drawing, painting, sculpture, and performance.
courses.prerequisites_text: senior standing. Open to media, studio, ICAM, and speculative design majors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Installation: Cross-Disciplinary Projects
courses.description: This course for the advanced visual arts major expands the idea contained in a singular work, or object, into the use of multiple objects, images, and media that redefines the idea as well as the space for which it is intended. Examination of historic, modern, and contemporary works will influence discussion of student project development and execution. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: senior standing. Open to media, studio, ICAM, and speculative design majors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Performing for the Camera
courses.description: This is a studio art course for the advanced visual arts major that explores the relationship between performance and the camera. From the selfie, performance documentation, and directing actors, this course explores standing in front of, between, and behind the lens.
courses.prerequisites_text: senior standing.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Studio Honors II
courses.description: The second advanced studio course in the Honors Program in Studio, the successful completion of which will lead toward an honors degree in the studio major. The course builds on the critical and technical issues raised in Studio Honors I.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 110M.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Church and Mosque: Medieval Art and Architecture between Christianity and Islam
courses.description: This course surveys the changes in art and architecture caused by the rise of new religions after the ancient world demise, a period of upheaval and contention often known as the “Clash of Gods.” How did Christianity come to dominate Europe with its churches and monasteries and then Islam with its mosques in the Middle East and North Africa? Studying the role of religion in the formation of artistic styles will show a dynamic interaction between the visual cultures of Christianity and Islam. Recommended preparation: VIS 20.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Arts of Japan
courses.description: Course is a survey of the visual arts of Japan, considering how the arts developed in the context of Japan’s history and discussing how art and architecture were used for philosophical, religious, and material ends. Recommended preparation: VIS 21B.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Seminar in Art History of Asia
courses.description: A seminar on an advanced topic of special interest in India, China, and Japan.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 112 or two upper-division courses in art history (VIS 113AN–129F).

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Seminar in Art Theory and Criticism
courses.description: A seminar on an advanced topic of special interest in art theory, art criticism, or the history of literature on art.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 112 or two upper-division courses in art history (VIS 113AN–129F).

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Studio Topics in Speculative Design
courses.description: A seminar that examines a topic of special interest in speculative design that is not addressed in the regular curriculum. Students will read, write, and produce work through projects. Topics will vary. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 30 or VIS 41. Open to media, studio, ICAM, and speculative design majors and speculative design minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to 3-D Asset Design
courses.description: This course teaches foundational skills in 3-D modeling, rendering, and animation to prepare students for specialized courses in architectural and urban design, virtual reality and augmented reality, virtual environments, computer gaming, character design, industrial design, and other applications. Emphasis is on a general understanding of widely used software and development of projects in an artistic and design context.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Computer Programming for the Arts II
courses.description: Students extend their programming capabilities to include the creation of reusable software libraries, packages, database APIs, tools, utilities, and applications intended to be publishable and useful to other practicing artists, or as preparatory work for the student’s senior thesis sequence. Two production-course limitation. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 141A. Open to ICAM and speculative design majors and minors only.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Time- and Process-Based Digital Media II
courses.description: Students will implement time- and process-based projects under direction of faculty. Projects such as software and hardware interfacing, computer mediated performance, software art, installation, interactive environments, data visualization and sonification will be produced as advanced study and portfolio project. Program or materials fees may apply. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 145A or ICAM 102. Open to ICAM and speculative design majors and computing and the arts and speculative design minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Computer-controlled Fabrication in Art I
courses.description: 2-D and 3-D digital fabrication with an overview of related contemporary art practices. Topics may include 3-D CAD software, laser etching and cutting, paint application (spray booth, powder baking), fabric technologies, additive 3-D printing, and other resources relevant to maker spaces.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 142. Open to ICAM and speculative design majors and computing and the arts and speculative design minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Computer-controlled Fabrication in Art II
courses.description: Critique-based, studio continuation of VIS 146A. Advanced topics in computer-controlled manufacturing and subtractive multi-axis CNC technologies. Includes survey of emerging or esoteric fabrication technologies and advanced 3-D CAD design for outsourcing to commercial and specialist fabricators.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 146A. Open to ICAM and speculative design majors and computing and the arts and speculative design minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Electronic Technologies for Art I
courses.description: Develop artworks and installations that utilize digital electronics. Techniques in digital electronic construction and computer interfacing for interactive control of sound, lighting, and electromechanics. Construction of devices that responsively adapt artworks to conditions involving viewer participation, space activation, machine intelligence. Recommended preparation: CSE 8A strongly recommended. Program or materials fees may apply. Purchase of components kit required. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 41 or VIS 70N or VIS 80. Open to media, studio, ICAM, and speculative design majors and computing and the arts and speculative design minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Seminar in Contemporary Computer Topics
courses.description: Topics relevant to computer-based art and music making, such as computer methods for making art/music, design of interactive systems, spatialization of visual/musical elements, critical studies. Topics will vary. May be taken for credit three times. Recommended preparation: VIS 145A or MUS 171. Program or materials fees may apply. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Open to media, studio, ICAM, and speculative design majors and ICAM and speculative design minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Landmarks of World Cinema
courses.description: A survey course on the most significant works of world cinema. Styles, genres, and national cinemas will be examined in comparative relation. Emphasis will be placed on collective film viewing, in-class discussion, and formal and/or narrative analysis.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Black Subjects and Black Material in Photography
courses.description: Thematic course asks how modernity’s concept of blackness might be bound to the emergence of photographic technologies and the trajectory and futures of Black peoples. Explores blackness as a fundamental element of photographic viewing—Black subjects as constituted within systems of political power and Black and queer subjectivities as places to locate contemporary critique. Investigations of these ideas will cover historical and contemporary photo media including art documentary and vernacular imagery.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 60 or VIS 83.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: History of Art and Technology
courses.description: Aims to provide historical context for computer arts by examining the interaction between the arts, media technologies, and sciences in different historical periods. Topics vary (e.g., Renaissance perspective, futurism and technology, and computer art of the 1950s and 1960s). Materials fees required.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Senior Project in Computing Arts I
courses.description: Students pursue projects of their own design over two quarters with support from faculty in a seminar environment. Project proposals are developed, informed by project development guidelines from real-world examples. Two production-course limitation. Renumbered from ICAM 160A. Students may receive credit for only one of the following: VIS 160A, MUS 160A, or ICAM 160A.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 145A and one course from VIS 141B or VIS 145B or VIS 147B or MUS 172. Open to ICAM majors only. Department stamp required.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Senior Project in Computing Arts II
courses.description: Continuation of VIS 160A or MUS 160A. Completion and presentation of independent projects along with documentation. Two production-course limitation. Renumbered from ICAM 160B. Students may receive credit for only one of the following: VIS 160B, MUS 160B, or ICAM 160B.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 160A or MUS 160A. Open to ICAM majors only.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Photographic Strategies: Looking and Seeing
courses.description: Course guides students in the discovery of the possibilities for making new work within specific photographic restrictions. Photography is approached through experimentation, failure, breakthroughs, and inspiration. We will explore ways of thinking and producing, cultivating a rigorous process for students to develop a meaningful way of making their work. The construction of sequences, series, and the art of editing will be an important part of this critique-based course. Program or materials fees may apply. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 60. Open to art history and criticism, media, studio, and ICAM majors and photography minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: The Photographic Print
courses.description: This course continues the student’s work of photographic printing with digital technology, with regard to the potentials of various print media and the way in which printing, editing, and sequence contribute to making meaning. Through demonstrations and workshops, lessons will include inkjet printing, alternative materials, scanning, and digital output of film. Students will be required to create a portfolio of prints. Program or materials fees may apply. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 60. Open to art history and criticism, media, studio, and ICAM majors and photography minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Social Engagement and Photography
courses.description: This course will explore the use of photography as a tool to both understand and represent the social world. Students will look critically at the historical claims of photography as evidence and as a tool of empirical knowledge and engage with the ethics of care and responsibility bound to visual representation. Students will develop a photo-based project that engages the social in a creative and critical way. Program or materials fees may apply. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 164 or VIS 165. Open to media, studio, and ICAM majors and photography minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Photography in Exhibition and Artist Books
courses.description: Focus on the preparation of photography for exhibition, including artist books, portfolios, or experimental and hybrid forms. How does exhibition and publishing contribute to the meaning and reception of photo-based work? Class includes workshops on file finishing and printing, framing, zine and artist bookmaking, and more. Students will visit exhibits in the San Diego-Los Angeles area. Students should have work-in-progress to examine. Program or materials fees may apply. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 165 or VIS 165A or VIS 165B. Open to media, studio, and ICAM majors and photography and digital film production minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Media Sketchbook
courses.description: Video medium used both as production technology and as device to explore the fundamental character of filmmaking and time-based computer art practices. Students perform all aspects of production with attention to developing ideas and building analytical/critical skills. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 70N. Open to media, studio, ICAM, speculative design, and cinematic arts majors; and film production and speculative design minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Sound: Theory and Practice
courses.description: Sound design is an essential component of media production and has opened up new structural possibilities for creative strategies in media arts. Students will encounter a critical and historical review of sound art, design, and production methodology. Critical papers and sound work for short projects will be required. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 174. Open to media, speculative design, and cinematic arts majors and film production minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Intermediate Projects in Media
courses.description: Topic based production course for media students with topics relevant to photography, video, film, and sound. Specific content will vary each quarter. May be taken for credit two times. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 174. Open to media and speculative design majors and film production minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Fiction and Allegory in Current Media Practices
courses.description: Course that theoretically and technically parses out how we create meaning through storytelling. How is history implicated in our experience of watching fiction? How does this affect the way that we create as artists? Students will examine the connection between the contrived and the real and language’s place in this cycle. There are both group-based and individual projects produced in this class around these issues. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 174 and two from VIS 164, 165, 165A, 165B, 171, 172, 175, 176, 177, 178, 179. Open to media majors only.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Advanced Sound and Lighting
courses.description: Advanced course to gain sophisticated control of lighting and sound recording techniques with understanding of theoretical implications and interrelation between production values and subject matter. Interactions between sound and image in various works in film, video, or installation. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 174 and two from VIS 164, 165, 165A, 165B, 171, 172, 175, 176, 177, 178, 179. Open to media majors only.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Strategies of Alterity
courses.description: An advanced production course which emphasizes how artists and filmmakers approach “otherness” and “difference” as it is constructed in various media practices. Course will examine a wide range of forms and genres such as ethnography, science fiction, crime narratives, documentary film, and animated shorts. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 174 and two from VIS 164, 165, 165A, 165B, 171, 172, 175, 176, 177, 178, 179. Open to media majors only.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Senior Media Projects
courses.description: Through instruction and discussion, the class will focus on guiding students through advanced production on a senior project. Students will be expected to initiate and complete production on at least one portfolio-level project. May be taken for credit two times. Two production-course limitation.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 174 and two from VIS 164, 165, 165A, 165B, 171, 172, 175, 176, 177, 178, 179. Open to media majors with senior standing only.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Design Master Studio
courses.description: This advanced course provides students with a unique immersive learning experience, based on design studio/atelier methods. This course develops students’ skills in the ideation, planning, and execution of complex individual and collaborative projects, including historical and contextual research, project ideation, planning and management, coordination of skills and responsibilities, iterative execution, and effective presentation.
courses.prerequisites_text: senior standing, VIS 135, and two from VIS 100A, VIS 101A, VIS 133A, VIS 136A, VIS 161, VIS 162.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Media Honors Thesis
courses.description: This advanced-level sequence coordinates three consecutive independent research courses to culminate in a completed thesis project in the third quarter of study. After the project’s public presentation, the faculty involved in the project will determine whether the student will graduate with departmental honors.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. Note: Requires a written proposal, 3.5 GPA in the major, prior consent from all involved, and approvals by the department chair and provost.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Special Studies in the Visual Arts
courses.description: Independent reading, research, or creative work under direction of a faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. Note: Open only to upper-division students. Requires instructor’s, department chair’s, and provost’s approval. Pass/Not Pass grades only.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Art Practice
courses.description: A workshop/seminar devoted to a particular materials practice (e.g., media, painting, digital media, etc.) that engages with critical questions arising within that discipline. Content will vary from quarter to quarter. May be taken for credit two times. (Required, MFA)

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Working Critique
courses.description: Workshop in which students engage in an extensive evaluation of one another’s ongoing work in preparation for either the First Year Review or MFA Review. Offered every winter. May be taken for credit two times (Required, MFA)

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Seminar in Art Practice Research
courses.description: Seminar examines the interrelationship between theory and practice and the nature of artistic production as a form of research.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. (Required for PhD in art practice concentration.)

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Thesis Exhibition
courses.description: Each student will be asked to explore a broad range of strategies for publicly presenting their work beyond the studio. This course includes research and planning for the required thesis exhibition for MFA candidates in visual arts. A detailed proposal of the MFA thesis exhibition is required to complete this course. (Required, MFA)

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Special Topics in Art Practice/Theory
courses.description: Examines a topic of special interest to permanent and visiting faculty that is not addressed in the regular curriculum. As in other Art Practice/Theory seminars, students will both produce work and read and write critically about the topic. Topics will vary.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Seminar in Latin American Art
courses.description: Historical and theoretical problems in the art of Mexico, Central, and South America art from the colonial period to today, as well as from the Hispanic traditions of the American Southwest. May be taken three times for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Material Culture
courses.description: This course will sketch the lineaments of material culture studies, a field in the arena of visual studies that engages the issue, broadly framed, of how people and things interact. We will approach the topic on two levels: with a critical reading of the work of major thinkers, and with case studies based on the interests and expertise of the course leader.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Individual Studies for Graduate Students
courses.description: Individual research with the student’s individual faculty adviser in preparation for their comprehensive exhibitions for the MFA degree or qualifying exam for the PhD. These units are intended to be with the chair of the student’s review committee. For the MFA degree, these units can only be taken after completing the First Year Review. (Required, MFA, PhD)

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Graduate Research
courses.description: Graduate-level research under the direct guidance of a faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: Apprentice teaching in undergraduate courses given by the Department of Visual Arts. Graduate students are required to teach a minimum of one quarter (four units) within the department to fulfill degree requirements.

courses.subject: WCWP
courses.title: The Writing Course A
courses.description: A seminar-style course in reading and writing required of all Warren College students. The course emphasizes argumentation and critical writing based on sources. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: satisfaction of the UC Entry Level Writing Requirement and must be a Warren College student.

courses.subject: WCWP
courses.title: The Writing Course B
courses.description: A seminar-style course in reading and writing required of all Warren College students who have completed WCWP 10A. The course continues the emphasis on argumentation and critical writing based on sources. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: satisfaction of WCWP 10A and must be a Warren College student.

courses.subject: WCWP
courses.title: Academic Writing
courses.description: An upper-division workshop course in argumentation and research with particular attention to analyzing and constructing academic arguments. A course specially designed for and required of transfer students who enter Warren College through the TAG, IGETC, or another articulation agreement. The course must be taken for a letter grade to fulfill this requirement. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: junior/senior standing and must be a Warren College student.

courses.subject: WES
courses.title: Capstone Project: Wireless Embedded Systems
courses.description: Small teams will demonstrate their critical thinking, organization, and design skills in attacking a problem within the WES field. The groups may approach this project as consultants hired to develop a new type of embedded wireless device for a specific application. They may be responsible for designing the device and implementing a working prototype.

courses.subject: WES
